Mirror's Edge was probably one of the most innovative FPS games I've played in the last decade, though the game suffered from the fact that it didn't really seem to know whether it wanted to be a shooter or a jump & run (among other things) and it didn't quite pull off synergizing both concepts. What I'm most surprised about is that the game was released some 7 years ago and no other company has so far tried to take some lessons from that game and succeeded.

Dying Light was pretty good, though, but got a bit repetitive quite soon, though that wasn't so much because of the Mirror's Edge-inspired mechanics rather than the general game around those.

Truthfully I think the design space of first person shooters has been all but mined out. It's been with us as a genre for over 20 years. I've shot everyone with everything everywhere. And it's leaked into many other genres. RPG, horror, simulation.

I don't think we'll see something like Scream which took a the stale horror genre and turned it's tropes on it's head. I'm not sure you can play around with inverting tropes as much in games when the tropes are the gameplay itself. Although games like Portal and Blood Dragon are interesting efforts. But in the case of Portal, it ultimately is a very different game from an FPS, and Blood Dragon for all it's tongue in cheek quality was a very by the numbers FPS.

I think all that can really be done anymore is good execution of a strong concept. Or strive to develop genre defying games.

Most gun mechanics can be improved, it's almost laughable what we actually pay for in COD and other games. Like its some kind of fucking magic magazine that self reloads the used magazine after you throw it on the damn ground just because you pulled out and put away your combat knife. This kind of leads back to gun mechanics, overheating should not be a mechanic unless you have infinite ammo. Even then its questionable. The Saw can fire 100 5.56 rounds at, get this, 800 rds a minute and not burst into flames (surprise surprise). Were taking bullets that are over 5 inches long with the casing, COD peeps imagine that shit. Most guns are designed to shoot lots of bullets very fast. If they are prone to overheating you will see critical failure before you would see the "gun shoot slower to stop overheat" mechanic. For some reason however, guns with rotating barrels are the worst when it comes to heat, and that makes even LESS sense. The rotating barrels are to reduce heat, a 3 barreled gun shooting will generate 1/3 the heat per barrel than a single barreled weapon. If the receiver wasn't designed to handle the heat as well, then they wouldn't have put a fucking rotating barrel on it.

Now to magazines/clips. THERE IS A LOT OF THEM. There are standards but also custom/modified magazines, for larger/smaller sizes. Yes it makes it heavier, but there is no standard 20 rd/30 rd extended mag. Shit the AA12 has a 50 rd magazine you can throw on it. 50 FUCKING SHOTGUN SHELLS DON'T LIMIT ME AT 10 YOU ASSHATS. Wtf, give us a slider or some shit. The more bulllets you have the worse your handling is. That would be tits, but it would also apparently be too hard.

Is it broke? only when your TTK is less than your latency (looking at you COD) if it took 8 shotgun shells of 50 to kill someone it would be fucking balanced. Change your balance or don't put it in, you can't have your cake and eat it too. Its bad enough almost all shotguns in games have absolutely terrible range and take up waaaay to much space on the screen, but my bullets also dissapear after a certain range. Why do so many games do this. Have they not gone trap shooting?

Lastly Include the actual stats for the weapons. Damage ranges, damage dropoff range, ROF, MOA for precision, view kick, alternate rounds, etc. Not random ass bars that don't mean shit. Get the terminology right here as well, accuracy is depends on the player, not the gun. Accuracy and Precision are not the same thing, look it up, its science bitch.

In short what do FPS games need to be innovative? Have the designers figure out how guns work, and go from there. I don't care if its a futuristic weapon, or has really low dmg for bullet size. Just don't be idiots... Not hard considering most have a multi-million dollar budget. All of the above is why WOT is popular and it's an arcade style game F2P Grindfest.
